minutes.headline: Commission approved two septic projects and heard a restoration plan for 675 Reservoir Road, sending delinquent fines to counsel.
minutes.summary: The Conservation Commission issued a standard order of conditions for a septic system at 140 Peninsula Drive and a negative determination for a septic repair at 453 Mass Ave. It held a working session on the 675 Reservoir Road restoration plan, where members pressed for more and larger trees before the notice of intent proceeds. It also voted to send the unpaid-fines question to the land use director and town counsel, and heard agent reports on enforcement matters, a state appeal and the trail budget.

public_comment.topic: Chair asked for public comment; none was offered.
An audience member asked about procedure for public comment on the continued hearing and whether they could stay for the Woodlands item.

votes.motion: Issue a standard order of conditions for the notice of intent at 140 Peninsula Drive.
Issue a negative 3 determination for the request for determination at 453 Mass Ave.
Continue the 675 Reservoir Road hearing to March 1st.
Forward the fine issue to the land use director and town counsel to determine whether the town can lien a property for delinquent fines.

budget_items.what_was_said: The advertising budget is used up, so the agent bills applicants for the legal-ad cost charged by the newspaper.
A member recalled the commission voting a daily fine until the front hill was stabilized.
Members want trail materials money restored after the snowmobile club stopped paying for trail work, and the agent will follow up with the town manager.
Members discussed fines of a few hundred dollars a day if conditions are not met by the April deadline.

decisions.decision: 554 Lancaster Avenue insignificant change remains continued to March 1st; the agent will ask the applicant's engineer for the flow rates.

675 Reservoir Road applicant will submit a restoration plan, site development plan and landscaping plan about the Friday before the next meeting; the restoration is limited to the area up to the 50-foot buffer and the flood plain, with hill planting handled under the notice of intent.
The Woodlands application will be on the March 1st agenda as a public meeting.
Whitman and Bingham will submit a remediation plan for 338 Sunset by the 17th for the March 1st meeting.
Approval of the minutes was held so the 183 Hemlock fine can be reviewed and added.
Agent will send the 12 West Street appeal document and notify members when the state site visit is scheduled.
Commission will wait until spring to look at the Sunny Hill Road land offered by Bill Drum.

what_happened.line: The Conservation Commission voted to send the question of liening properties for unpaid fines to the land use director and town counsel.
The commission issued a standard order of conditions for the septic system notice of intent at 140 Peninsula Drive.
A negative determination was issued unanimously for the septic repair at 453 Mass Ave.
The 675 Reservoir Road restoration plan had a working session; the applicant will submit plans before the hearing, continued to March 1st.
The agent said the advertising budget is used up, so applicants are billed for legal-ad costs, and members want trail materials money restored.

why_it_matters: Whether the town can place a lien for delinquent conservation fines decides if unpaid penalties can be collected through the property, which affects how enforcement at sites like 675 Reservoir Road and 183 Hemlock is backed.
With the advertising line exhausted, applicants pay legal-ad costs directly, and trail upkeep now depends on a budget line that members want restored after outside funding ended.
watch_next: March 1st meeting: continued 675 Reservoir Road hearing, 554 Lancaster Avenue, the Woodlands public meeting and the 338 Sunset remediation plan.
Reply from the land use director and town counsel on whether the town can lien a property for delinquent fines.
